transcript: The Lost Boys has been getting a lot of attention for the sheer number of changes that it is made over the course of the preview period. And as someone who saw the show in a very early previews, I was excited to go back post opening now that the show is frozen, to see what changes were made and if it changed my opinion on the show. Because when I first saw it I was definitely mixed to positive. I thought the effects and spectacle were obviously amazing, and I thought it was a pretty strong adaptation of the film that just didn't quite stick the landing for me. And I am happy to report that a lot of the changes made did indeed make the show better. My two least favourite songs in the show were either cut or replaced with a new song. The show is tighter, running about 15 minutes shorter than when I first saw it, and one of the main character deaths now feels much more significant. However, I do feel like my overall sentiments remain the same. I do feel like they succeeded in adding a ton of depth to a story that was mostly vibes in the film, but I do find the overall pacing of the show to be a bit wonky. Act one kind of drags its feet a bit so that the big transformation can be its Act 1 finale set piece, and Act 2 seemingly abandons our main Character of Michael for a good majority of its run time, instead shifting focus to our younger brother character played by Benjamin Pajak. And while I thought Pajak was great, the character as written is essentially just a walking gay stereotype, with a lot of the jokes surrounding the character being ha ha, isn't it funny that he notices what shoes people are wearing Or has a poster of Rob Lowe in his closet? And so I didn't love the way that the show handled that character's queerness. Although if you ask director Michael Arden, he may not even be gay at all. Because, and I quote, the rainbow means a lot of different things to many people. But despite the lack of depth given to the character of Sam, I was pleasantly surprised to see that the character of Lucy, our mother character played by Shoshana Bean, is given a ton of depth and agency that she did not have in the film. And of course, Shoshana Bean sings the hell out of it, despite the songs that they give her being just kind of okay. I do think that the best songs in the show are those given to David and the Lost Boys, who in this version of the story are not just a gang of vampires, but also a rock band, a change that actually works surprisingly well. And Ali Louis Bourzgui, who plays David, the leader of the Lost Boys, is, in my opinion, giving the Standout performance of the show. He is just such a magnetic performer and manages to perfectly balance a performance that is both an homage to kiefer Sutherland in the film while also making it completely his own. Ultimately, I do think that despite some of the pitfalls in the book and score, this is undeniably an impressive and entertaining production. And there are people out there making the show out to be the worst thing they've ever seen, or an affront to Broadway. And to those people I say, have you seen other shows? this show is far from perfect, but if this is the worst thing you've ever seen, then I am insanely jealous of you, as despite some of its issues, this is still going to get a Broadway Ben recommendation.
